text: Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah[1] walked around in the flames, singing praises to the Lord God.
Then Azariah stood still and prayed out loud:
You, Lord God of our ancestors, are worthy to be praised, and your name should be honored forever.
Everything you do is right; your decisions bring justice.
You were right to punish us and to destroy holy Jerusalem, the city of our ancestors. Our people have sinned;
we have broken all your laws and turned away from you.
We have disobeyed, even though your commands were for our own good.
You were right to punish us
and to let us be conquered by our hateful enemies. They refuse to obey your Law, and the most evil king on earth is their ruler.
They insult us, your servants. We are a disgrace and have no excuse. But we worship and obey you.
Please, Lord, for the sake of your reputation, keep your agreement with us, and someday set us free.
You loved Abraham; Isaac obeyed you, and you chose Jacob.[2] For their sakes, don't take your mercy from us.
You promised to give them more descendants than there are stars in the sky or grains of sand on a beach.
But we sinned, and so we have become the smallest nation. We are ashamed
because we have no rulers, no prophets, no leaders. We have no incense, no altar, and no sacrifices to please you or to ask for your mercy.
But if we are humble and truly sorry for our sins,

you will accept us as if we had offered a thousand rams and bulls and ten thousand fat lambs. You never disappoint those who trust you, Lord. We want to be your followers,[3] so please answer our prayer.
We promise with all our hearts to worship and obey you and to continue praying.
So please be patient with us and show us your mercy.
Work a miracle and rescue us, so that you, Lord, will be honored.
We, your servants, pray that those who have harmed us will be disgraced; crush their mighty power so they will fail.
Show them that you alone are the glorious Lord God, the Ruler of all the earth.
After the king's servants threw Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah into the furnace, the servants kept tossing in oil, tar, dried flax plants, and small pieces of firewood.
The flames blazed up 22 meters above the furnace,
and they also shot out from the furnace and burned the Babylonians who were standing nearby.
But one of the Lord's angels came down into the furnace to protect Azariah and his two friends. The angel forced the flames out of the furnace,
so that the inside of the furnace felt as if a cool breeze were blowing. The fire didn't touch the three men at all, and it caused them no pain or trouble.
Then Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah praised God together in the furnace, and they sang:
You, Lord God of our ancestors, are always worthy to be praised.
Your glorious and holy name will always deserve the greatest honor.
So let songs of praise be sung in your holy temple for all time. *
There, from your throne above the winged creatures,
you watch everything on earth and rule the world with glory and majesty. We pray that your praises will be sung forever.
And age after age in the starry skies, songs will be sung to honor you. Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah continued to sing:
All of creation should sing praises to the Lord forever. *
Everything in the heavens and the water above the sky *
should sing praises to the Lord forever. *
The angels and the rulers in the heavens
should sing praises to the Lord forever. *
The sun, the moon,
and the stars should sing praises to the Lord forever. *
The wind and the rain
and the dew, *
as well as the freezing snow, *
and the fiery heat
should sing praises to the Lord forever. *
The dark of night and the light of day
should sing praises to the Lord forever. *
The frost and snow, *
the icy cold,
and the thunderstorms should sing praises to the Lord forever.[4]
Everything on this earth should sing praises to the Lord forever. *
The mountains and hills
and all trees and plants should sing praises to the Lord forever. *
The springs and rivers, *
together with the oceans
and every sea creature, whether large or small, should sing praises to the Lord forever. *
Each bird in the sky,
and every animal, wild or tame, should sing praises to the Lord forever.
Every human should sing praises to the Lord forever, *
especially his priests
and his chosen people. *
We humans should be humble *
and obey the Lord
with all our heart and soul, and we should sing praises to him forever.

The three of us— Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael— should sing praises to the Lord forever, because if he hadn't rescued us, we would have died in a flaming furnace and gone down to the world of the dead.
So praise the Lord for his goodness, and praise him for his mercy, because it will never end.
Everyone who worships the Lord, the Supreme God, should sing his praises and thank him for his mercy, because it will never end.
